question: The primary clinical duty of a nurse regarding hospital tools is what?
explanation: Nurses act as primary daily users responsible for safe handling and stewardship in the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why must ward nurses inspect medical tools routinely before starting their shifts?

options.B: To prevent sudden device breakdowns during medical emergencies
options.C: To fulfill insurance requirements for the hospital building
options.D: To calculate the total financial value of the ward

explanation: Routine checks ensure instruments work properly when critical care situations arise. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h1)

question: A nebulizer used to treat a patient having an asthma attack belongs to which category?
explanation: Apparatus used to treat illnesses and administer active interventions fall under therapeutic tools. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main characteristic of consumable hospital materials?

options.A: They are discarded immediately after a single patient use
options.B: They are exclusively kept in the hospital theater
options.C: They last for several years without needing replacement
options.D: They require electrical power to function properly

explanation: Consumables are designed for single-use applications to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the correct way to disconnect an electrical device from the wall socket?

options.A: Switch off the main power breaker
options.C: Pull firmly on the flexible cord
options.D: Jerk the cable from a distance

explanation: Pulling by the plug prevents internal wire strain and electrical hazards. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: A nurse is moving a heavy oxygen cylinder down the ward corridor. What safety action is required?

options.A: Carry it on the shoulder to save time
options.B: Leave it unsecuring in the middle of the hallway
options.C: Roll it rapidly across rough concrete floors
options.D: Engage safety transport locks and use ramps

explanation: Secure transport prevents heavy cylinders from tipping over and causing severe injury. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which processing step must always be performed FIRST before disinfection and sterilization?
explanation: Cleaning removes organic debris that otherwise protects microorganisms from subsequent germ-killing processes. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: Which medical device level requires complete sterilization using pressurized steam?

options.A: Plastic basins used for routine bed baths
options.B: Bedside tables touched by visiting relatives
options.C: Surgical forceps entering sterile body tissues
options.D: Rubber tubing used for non-invasive oxygen delivery

explanation: Items entering sterile tissues or the vascular system demand complete destruction of all microbial spores. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h4)

question: What environmental condition can cause rapid degradation of sensitive hospital electronics?
explanation: Excessive moisture promotes rust, short circuits, and mold growth on delicate electronic components. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses participate in regular ward equipment stock audits?

options.A: To evaluate the architectural strength of the ward building
options.B: To calculate monthly staff salaries for the hospital accounts department
options.C: To reconcile physical items against inventory records and find missing tools
options.D: To design new medical devices for local manufacturing firms

explanation: Audits ensure all assigned assets are accounted for and ready for clinical deployment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a major vector for spreading nosocomial infections across a hospital ward?

options.A: Storing equipment in dry and clean cabinets
options.B: Proper handwashing before every patient contact
options.C: Using sterile disposable syringes only once

explanation: Shared devices transferred between patients without cleaning carry infectious agents easily. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which practice is NOT effective for decontaminating a blood pressure cuff used between patients?

options.A: Scrubbing away organic soil before disinfection
options.B: Allowing the recommended wet contact time to elapse
options.C: Using an approved chemical disinfectant wipe
options.D: Wiping the cuff surface with a dry cotton cloth

explanation: Dry wiping fails to remove micro-organisms and lacks the chemical action required for true disinfection. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h6)

question: What immediate action must a nurse take upon finding a broken infusion pump?

options.A: Hide it inside a bedside locker until next week
options.B: Leave it plugged in for the next shift to discover
options.C: Tag it out of order and remove it from the active ward
options.D: Attempt to solder the internal circuit board alone

explanation: Immediate tagging and removal prevent accidental clinical use of a compromised device. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h7)

question: Why should ward nurses avoid attempting DIY repairs on damaged electrical equipment?

options.A: It saves the hospital too much money on technicians
options.B: It improves the overall warranty coverage of the asset
options.C: It speeds up the return of the device to clinical use
options.D: It creates severe electrocution and fire hazards

explanation: Unauthorized repairs by unqualified personnel increase safety risks and violate hospital policy. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T1#GNS112_U4_T1_h7)
